answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents tie identities to a cryptographic attestation chain verified by zero-knowledge proofs. Each validated action weaves into an execution thread, where verification fees scale superlinearly. A rogue cluster cannot fake proof of agenthood without exponential capital exhaustion: spam attempts echo back as soaring staking penalties, while benign nodes draw resilience from decentralized trust roots like resilient yarrow in harsh soil.
